note: Standard-weight (Ws) equations in metric form: log10(W, grams) = a + b × log10(TL, millimeters), where TL is total length. Ws is the 75th-percentile weight at a given length across many populations of the species, so it describes a well-fed, above-average fish, not an average one. Relative weight Wr = 100 × actual weight / Ws: about 100 is a well-conditioned fish, 85 is thin, 115 is heavy (pre-spawn females, fish on rich forage). Equations only apply at or above minTLmm (and at or below maxTLmm where given); weights for very large fish are extrapolations because few trophies are in the data sets. Coefficients were taken from the WSlit table in the FSA R package (Ogle et al.), whose documentation states that most equations can be found in, and its sources match, Neumann, Guy & Willis (2012), 'Length, weight, and associated indices', Fisheries Techniques, 3rd ed., American Fisheries Society. Cross-checks: largemouth b = 3.273 (Henson 1991) also appears in the Wikipedia 'Standard weight in fish' article; walleye -5.453 / 3.180 appears in the FSAWs package documentation; bluegill -5.374 / 3.316 appears in the Texas A&M AgriLife fish population assessment handout.
